title: I published a Halloween game in 12 hours on itch. My biggest lessons.
author: Teddydestroyer
selftext:
I spent about 12 hours building \*Trick or Trick?\*, a 3D Halloween fast paced deduction game.

I want to see how far I could take an idea in a single day.

A few things I learned:

\- Spend your time on what makes the game interesting. I didn’t want to spend hours designing the space, so I 3D generated the entire stylised room at one go and focus on gameplay.  
\- Good assets don’t automatically make a good game, but a bad asset would not have captured it either. Make sure assets are good enough.  
\- Working beats perfect during a short build. One character was fully rigged, but its animations were rough. That was good enough to test the idea and keep moving.  
\- Make balancing easy to change. Being able to adjust values quickly helped me test and improve the experience. Do not vibe code your way to balancing.  
\- Publish the imperfect version. Get it out there for feedback asap. It’s easy to keep starting projects and never finish them. Getting something playable out there is a habit you need to build.

I would love to hear what you think of the game, feedbacks appreciated.  
Play it: [https://virtical.itch.io/trick-or-threat](https://virtical.itch.io/trick-or-threat)    
Build walkthrough: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tr\_TZZ56Jg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tr_TZZ56Jg)

comments.body: I have no idea what I'm looking at, at a glance, but I see pumpkins, Halloween, and someone cranking pumpkins out in a single day, apparently. That's all that matters in the end.
